title: Successive minimal-area divisions leave quadrilateral cells forming an epidermis

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Successive minimal-area divisions leave quadrilateral cells forming an epidermis

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Successive minimal-area divisions of a disc soon leave only quadrilateral cells at the periphery, which divide radially, producing a superficial layer of parallel-sided cells (an epidermis) contrasting with the irregular cells beneath.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. VIII: The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: we shall consequently have a superficial or peripheral layer of quadrilateral cells, with sides approximately parallel, that is to say what we are accustomed to call _an epidermis_.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter VIII, “The Forms of Tissues, or Cell-Aggregates (continued)”; topic “Origin of an epidermis by minimal-area division”. Scope: discoid and rounded embryonic structures of plants (moss embryos, algal discs, antheridia)

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch08-07: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.62

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The proposed topological sequence is measurable in time-lapse images. Existing developmental data can test restricted plant systems, but they do not broadly isolate minimal-area division as the cause of epidermis formation.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: From lineage-resolved disc growth, test whether successive near-minimal divisions preferentially leave quadrilateral peripheral cells that divide radially and form a parallel-sided outer layer.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Lineage-resolved data for the named algae and cryptogams are limited.

Epidermal identity may also be specified molecularly.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The finished pattern, a superficial file of parallel-sided cells, is visible in some open embryo volumes. Showing that the pattern is the residue of minimal-area divisions needs the division sequence or a model comparison tied to those cells. Existing data can check the pattern in a few systems and only partly test the proposed mechanism.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In discoid embryos, algal discs and antheridia, test whether repeated divisions leave a peripheral layer of quadrilateral cells with radial walls, and whether a minimal-area division sequence reproduces that layer. A peripheral quadrilateral epidermis generated by that sequence would support the claim; a peripheral layer whose divisions do not follow the minimal-area order would weaken the proposed origin.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A quadrilateral epidermis can be produced by an identity program as well as by successive least-area divisions.

Moss embryos, algal discs and antheridia are sparsely represented next to Arabidopsis.
